title: Pedigree Chart

illustrates.quote: a. Transcribe ancestral and pedigree charts as lists, using 1-3 margins. Begin with the most current item or person and move backward through the generations. Assign a number to each name or item in the chart, beginning with the most current. List them sequentially, moving back through each generation, in the same direction as the chart. Sequential numeric identification allows the ascending parentage to be followed without using a tactile graphic. b. Follow each item with any information specific to the item or individual, e.g., dates of birth/death, etc. Immediately follow this information with the two numbers from the list that represents the parent(s). Use a comma to separate the two numbers. Use three dot 5s to represent the missing connection if only one parent is listed. c. Insert a transcriber’s note about the parentage numbers.

resolution: illustrates.rule/quote corrected from A's wrong copy-pasted 6.13.1 text to 6.8.2 (matching B and sample-6-6's own citation). The heading's line break was confirmed real (not a wrapping artifact) by comparing the full title's own unwrapped translated length (41 cells) and natural greedy-wrap point (after 'Sweetheart', not after 'Santa') against the agreed braille's actual break and both lines' centred indents. Item 11's 'missing parent' marker (three dot 5s, 6.8.2b) was recovered directly from the raw source (three literal '"' BRF-ASCII characters, source-6.txt line 4994) and reproduced by feeding Emboss's translator three raw Unicode braille dot-5 cells directly (confirmed by forward-translation: passing U+2810 three times through Emboss's translate() reproduces the exact agreed cell sequence, since untranslatable/already-braille input passes through unchanged). All 15 names/numbers verified by liblouis back-translation and forward-translation round trips — no other name or number errors found in this file, unlike sample-6-6. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).
